# Presets

A preset is a configuration that says where its criterion comes from. Use them in `extends`; later ones
win, and each is applied once. `crowded-folders init` proposes the ones that fit a repository, and
`crowded-folders presets` lists them in the terminal.

Where a guide gives a number, the preset uses it and quotes it. Where none does — most of them — the
limits are the ones measured over 30 real repositories ([field-trial.md](field-trial.md)): 20 modules is
about the 95th percentile of folder sizes, the biggest folder in twenty.

| Preset | Proposed by `init` |
| --- | --- |
| [`recommended`](#recommended) | Always. |
| [`strict`](#strict) | Never: add it yourself. |
| [`angular`](#angular) | When it finds a file matching `angular.json`, or a dependency on `@angular/core`. |
| [`react`](#react) | When it finds a dependency on `react` or `react-dom` or `react-native`. |
| [`nextjs`](#nextjs) | When it finds a dependency on `next`. |
| [`react-native`](#react-native) | When it finds a dependency on `react-native` or `expo`. |
| [`vue`](#vue) | When it finds a dependency on `vue` or `nuxt`. |
| [`nuxt`](#nuxt) | When it finds a file matching `nuxt.config.{ts,js,mjs,mts}`, or a dependency on `nuxt`. |
| [`svelte`](#svelte) | When it finds a dependency on `svelte` or `@sveltejs/kit`. |
| [`nestjs`](#nestjs) | When it finds a dependency on `@nestjs/core`. |
| [`python`](#python) | When it finds a file matching `pyproject.toml` or `setup.py` or `setup.cfg` or `requirements.txt` or `Pipfile`. |
| [`django`](#django) | When it finds a file matching `manage.py`. |

| [`android`](#android) | When it finds a file matching `AndroidManifest.xml`. |
| [`dotnet`](#dotnet) | When it finds a file matching `*.csproj` or `*.fsproj` or `*.vbproj` or `*.sln` or `*.slnx`. |

## recommended

The two rules that matter, at limits measured on real repositories: at most 20 modules in a folder (a module is a file with its companions: foo.ts, foo.spec.ts and foo.html are one), and 4 modules sharing a first word make a folder. Leaves out vendored, generated and test-data folders, changelog fragments, media, translations and the folders of tools (.github).

- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules","dotfiles":false}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"min":4,"words":1,"ignore":["test","tests","spec","get","set","is","has","can","should"]}`
- **`max-folders`:** `off`
- **`redundant-prefix`:** `off`
- **`single-file-folders`:** `off`
- **Left out:** `node_modules`, `vendor`, `third_party`, `third-party`, `*[fF]ixtures`, `__fixtures__`, `__snapshots__`, `[sS]napshots`, `[sS]creenshots`, `[gG]oldens`, `[eE]xpected`, `[tT]est[dD]ata`, `__mocks__`, `changelog`, `changelog.d`, `changelog_unreleased`, `newsfragments`, `.*`, `*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,webp,avif,ico,icns,bmp,tif,tiff,psd,xcf,exr,hdr,mp3,wav,ogg,flac,m4a,aac,mp4,webm,mov,avi,mkv,ttf,otf,woff,woff2,eot,pdf}`, `migrations`, `migrate`, `**/alembic/versions`, `**/db/migration`, `dist`, `coverage`, `__pycache__`, `.git`
- **In `**/locales`, `**/locale`, `**/i18n`, `**/l10n`, `**/translations`, `**/lang`, `**/langs`, `**/Localization`, `**/Localization/**`:** `max-files` `off`, `prefix-groups` `off`. Translations are one file per language, side by side by nature: en, en-GB and en-US are not a group to move.
- **In `.`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":40}`. The root holds what tools look for there on their own: manifests, lockfiles, licences, configs.

Sources:

- [Angular style guide: "consider splitting further"](https://angular.dev/style-guide#project-structure)
- [docs/presets.md: how the limits were measured](https://github.com/bymaksym/CrowdedFolders/blob/main/docs/presets.md)

## strict

Tighter than recommended: at most 12 modules in a folder, 3 modules sharing a prefix make a folder, at most 20 subfolders, no module repeating its folder's name, and no folder holding a single file. An opinion, not a measurement: use it when you want the tree tidier than most.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":12,"count":"modules"}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"min":3}`
- **`max-folders`:** `error` `{"max":20}`
- **`redundant-prefix`:** `error`
- **`single-file-folders`:** `warn`

Sources:

- [Angular style guide (former LIFT "Flat" rule: sub-folders at seven or more files)](https://github.com/kenny-chow-my/AngularStyleGuide)

## angular

Angular's own guide: folders by feature, a component's files together, and sub-folders once a folder of the app's src/ passes about ten — the old style guide said seven, and ten when it explained why. Counts a component and its template, styles and spec once. Scripts and tooling outside src/ keep recommended's limit.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Left out:** `.angular`, `src/environments`
- **In `**/src`, `**/src/**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":10,"count":"modules","hint":"Angular asks for folders by feature, not by type (no components/ or services/)."}`. The style guide is about the application code, which Angular puts in src/: "All of your Angular UI code (TypeScript, HTML, and styles) should live inside a directory named src".

Sources:

- [Angular style guide: project structure](https://angular.dev/style-guide)
- [Former Angular style guide, 04-04 "Flat": sub-folders at seven or more files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/17.3.x/aio/content/guide/styleguide.md)

## react

React has no official layout, so this is recommended plus what React names mean: `use` starts every hook and `with` many higher-order components, so they are skipped before reading what a file is about (useAuthLogin and AuthForm are both about auth). Counts a component with its test, story and styles once.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Leading words skipped:** `use`, `with`
- **Left out:** `public`

Sources:

- [React docs (legacy): file structure — "don't overthink it", at most three or four levels](https://legacy.reactjs.org/docs/faq-structure.html)
- [React: hook names must start with use](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks)
- [bulletproof-react: project structure by feature](https://github.com/alan2207/bulletproof-react/blob/master/docs/project-structure.md)

## nextjs

React, plus the App Router: under app/ a folder is a URL segment, so the advice is a private folder (_name) or a route group ((name)), which group files without changing URLs.

- **Extends:** [react](#react)
- **Left out:** `.next`, `next-env.d.ts`
- **In `app`, `app/**`, `src/app`, `src/app/**`:** `prefix-groups` `error` `{"hint":"Under app/ a folder is a URL segment: use a private folder (_name) or a route group ((name))."}`. Under the App Router a plain folder becomes part of the URL.

Sources:

- [Next.js: project structure, private folders and route groups](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure)

## react-native

React, plus the native projects: ios/ and android/ next to the app are the Xcode and Gradle projects that the template or Expo prebuild generates, not code arranged by hand, so they are left out wherever the app lives in the repository.

- **Extends:** [react](#react)
- **Left out:** `/ios`, `/android`, `.expo`

Sources:

- [Expo: continuous native generation — prebuild "creates the android and ios directories"](https://docs.expo.dev/workflow/continuous-native-generation/)

## vue

Vue's style guide asks for the opposite of prefix-groups in components/: tightly coupled children are named after their parent (TodoList, TodoListItem, TodoListItemButton) and kept flat, and sub-folders wait until about 100 components. So components/ gets no prefix groups and a high limit; Base, App and V are skipped as the prefixes of base components.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":30,"count":"modules"}`
- **Leading words skipped:** `base`, `app`, `v`, `the`, `use`
- **Left out:** `.nuxt`, `.output`
- **In `**/components`, `**/components/**`:** `prefix-groups` `off`, `max-files` `error` `{"max":100}`. The Vue style guide names coupled children after their parent and keeps them flat ("This isn't recommended" about nesting them), and only suggests sub-folders in "very large apps (e.g. 100+ components)".

Sources:

- [Vue style guide: tightly coupled component names, base component names, order of words](https://vuejs.org/style-guide/rules-strongly-recommended.html)

## nuxt

Vue, plus Nuxt's directories: composables/ and utils/ are auto-imported from their top level only, so a sub-folder there breaks imports unless it is re-exported, and in pages/ and server/ a file is a URL. Groups there are warnings that say so.

- **Extends:** [vue](#vue)
- **In `**/composables`, `**/utils`:** `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"hint":"Nuxt only auto-imports the top level here: a sub-folder needs an index that re-exports it, or imports.dirs in nuxt.config."}`. Nuxt auto-imports only the top level of composables/ and utils/: a file moved into a sub-folder stops being imported, silently.
- **In `**/pages`, `**/pages/**`, `**/server/api`, `**/server/api/**`, `**/server/routes/**`:** `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"hint":"Here a folder is part of the URL: moving a file changes its route."}`. In pages/ and server/ the path of a file is its URL, so grouping files into a folder changes their routes.

Sources:

- [Nuxt: composables, "Nuxt only scans files at the top level of the app/composables/ directory"](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/directory-structure/app/composables)
- [Nuxt: utils, scanned "identical to the app/composables/ directory"](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/directory-structure/app/utils)
- [Nuxt: server, "Files inside the ~~/server/api are automatically prefixed with /api in their route"](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/directory-structure/server)

## svelte

Recommended, plus SvelteKit routes: under src/routes a folder is a route, so the advice is a group folder ((name)). The + of route files (+page, +layout) is not a prefix.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Left out:** `.svelte-kit`, `static`
- **In `src/routes`, `src/routes/**`:** `prefix-groups` `error` `{"hint":"Under src/routes a folder is a route: use a group folder ((name)) to keep the URLs."}`. Under src/routes a plain folder becomes a route.

Sources:

- [SvelteKit: project structure](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/project-structure)
- [SvelteKit: routing (+ files, groups)](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/routing)

## nestjs

NestJS organises by module, one folder per feature (cats/cats.controller.ts, cats/cats.service.ts are one module). Recommended with modules counted once.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"hint":"NestJS groups a feature as a module folder."}`

Sources:

- [NestJS: modules](https://docs.nestjs.com/modules)

## python

Recommended, read the way pytest names tests: test_parser.py and parser_test.py are the module parser. tests/ mirrors the package, so it is not asked to group on its own — split the package and the tests follow.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Companions:** `^test_`, `_test$`, `_tests$`
- **Left out:** `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `venv`, `.tox`, `.nox`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `*.egg-info`
- **In `tests`, `tests/**`, `**/tests`, `**/tests/**`:** `prefix-groups` `off`. Tests mirror the package they test: when the package splits, they follow it.

Sources:

- [PEP 8: package and module names](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/)
- [pytest: good practices, test discovery (test_*.py or *_test.py)](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/explanation/goodpractices.html)

## django

Python, plus Django: each app keeps models.py, views.py, admin.py… side by side by convention, and migrations stay flat and numbered (Django's answer to too many is squashing, not folders).

- **Extends:** [python](#python)
- **Left out:** `/static`, `/media`, `/staticfiles`

Sources:

- [Django: applications](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/ref/applications/)
- [Django: migrations (squashing)](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/topics/migrations/)

## go

Go puts a package in a folder, and a new folder is a new package with its own API — so the limits are looser and the advice is about packages. Reads foo_test.go, foo_linux.go and foo_linux_amd64_test.go as foo. Go's own guidance: "There is no 'one type, one file' convention"; net/http has 17 files and the go command 34.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":30,"count":"modules","hint":"In Go a folder is a package: split off a part that has its own API, not just to shorten the list."}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"hint":"In Go a folder is a package: would they make sense as their own package?"}`
- **Companions:** `_test$`, `_(aix|android|darwin|dragonfly|freebsd|hurd|illumos|ios|js|linux|nacl|netbsd|openbsd|plan9|solaris|wasip1|windows|zos|unix)$`, `_(386|amd64|arm|arm64|loong64|mips|mipsle|mips64|mips64le|ppc64|ppc64le|riscv64|s390x|sparc64|wasm)$`
- **Left out:** `testdata`, `*.pb.go`, `*_string.go`, `zz_generated.*`

Sources:

- [Go: organizing a Go module](https://go.dev/doc/modules/layout)
- [Google Go style: package size](https://google.github.io/styleguide/go/best-practices)
- [The Go blog: organizing Go code](https://go.dev/blog/organizing-go-code)
- [go build: _test.go, testdata and build constraints in file names](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go)

## rust

Recommended for Rust: render_json.rs and render_pr.rs become render.rs and render/json.rs, the module layout the Rust reference prefers. Cargo builds one target per file in src/bin, examples, benches and tests, so those stay flat.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Left out:** `target`
- **In `**/src/bin`, `**/examples`, `**/benches`, `**/tests`, `**/tests/**`:** `max-files` `off`, `prefix-groups` `off`. Cargo makes every file there its own target (binary, example, benchmark, integration test), and UI-test suites keep one case per file.

Sources:

- [The Rust reference: modules and module source files](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/modules.html)
- [Cargo: package layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/project-layout.html)

## java

Java and Kotlin with Maven or Gradle: a folder is a package, so groups of classes sharing a name (UserService, UserRepository, UserController) suggest packaging by feature. UserServiceTest and UserServiceIT are read as UserService. One top-level class per file makes folders larger than in TypeScript, hence 20.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules","hint":"A folder is a package: package by feature (user/, order/), not by layer."}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"hint":"A folder is a package: they would be the package of that feature."}`
- **Companions:** `(Test|Tests|IT|IntegrationTest|Spec)$`
- **Left out:** `target`, `build`, `.gradle`, `generated`, `generated-sources`

Sources:

- [Maven: standard directory layout](https://maven.apache.org/guides/introduction/introduction-to-the-standard-directory-layout.html)
- [Google Java style guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html)
- [Kotlin coding conventions: directory structure](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/coding-conventions.html)
- [IntelliJ inspection: package with too many classes (50)](https://jetbrains.com/help/inspectopedia/PackageWithTooManyClasses.html)

## android

Java/Kotlin, plus Android resources: res/ folders cannot have sub-folders ("Alternative resource directories can't be nested"), so prefixes such as activity_, fragment_ and ic_ are the only grouping there is. res/ is left out.

- **Extends:** [java](#java)
- **Left out:** `**/src/*/res`, `/res`

Sources:

- [Android: providing resources](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/resources/providing-resources)
- [ribot Android guidelines: resource naming](https://github.com/ribot/android-guidelines/blob/master/project_and_code_guidelines.md)

## dotnet

C# and .NET: a folder is a namespace (IDE0130 is on by default), the I of an interface is not what it is about (IUserService belongs with UserService), and UserServiceTests is UserService. One type per file, hence 20.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules","hint":"In C# a folder is a namespace (IDE0130)."}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"hint":"In C# a folder is a namespace (IDE0130)."}`
- **Companions:** `^I(?=[A-Z])`, `(Tests|Test)$`
- **Leading words skipped:** `i`
- **Left out:** `bin`, `obj`, `Migrations`, `wwwroot/lib`, `Properties`, `.vs`

Sources:

- [IDE0130: namespace does not match folder structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/style-rules/ide0130)
- [C# identifier names: interfaces start with I](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/coding-style/identifier-names)

## swift

Swift and iOS: User+Codable.swift is an extension of User and belongs with it, and UserTests is User. Asset catalogs, localisation folders and Xcode bundles are left out.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Companions:** `\+.+$`, `(Tests|Test|Spec)$`
- **Left out:** `*.xcassets`, `*.lproj`, `*.xcodeproj`, `*.xcworkspace`, `DerivedData`, `Pods`, `Carthage`, `.build`

Sources:

- [Google Swift style guide: file names (MyType+MyProtocol.swift)](https://google.github.io/swift/)

## flutter

Flutter and Dart: feature-first under lib/ui, foo_test.dart is foo, and the generated platform folders and localisation files are left out. Flutter's own architecture guide organises lib/data by type on purpose, so it is given more room.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Companions:** `_test$`
- **Left out:** `.dart_tool`, `/build`, `/android`, `/ios`, `/web`, `/windows`, `/linux`, `/macos`, `**/lib/l10n`, `**/lib/generated`, `*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`
- **In `lib/data/**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":30}`, `prefix-groups` `warn`. The Flutter architecture guide organises the data layer by type: "The data folder organizes code by type".

Sources:

- [Effective Dart: style (file names)](https://dart.dev/effective-dart/style)
- [Flutter: app architecture case study (ui by feature, data by type)](https://docs.flutter.dev/app-architecture/case-study)
- [json_serializable: generated code goes in a part file, part 'example.g.dart'](https://pub.dev/packages/json_serializable)

## rails

Ruby on Rails organises app/ by type by design, and every sub-folder is a Zeitwerk namespace (app/models/admin/role.rb is Admin::Role): app/models, controllers, jobs, mailers and helpers get more room, and groups there are warnings that suggest a namespace. user_test.rb and user_spec.rb are user.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules"}`
- **Companions:** `_(test|spec)$`
- **Left out:** `/tmp`, `/log`, `/storage`, `/public`, `app/assets/builds`, `db/schema.rb`
- **In `app/{models,controllers,jobs,mailers,helpers,policies,serializers,services,workers,validators,presenters}`, `app/{models,controllers,jobs,mailers,helpers,policies,serializers,services,workers,validators,presenters}/**`, `app/views/**`, `spec/**`, `test/**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":40}`, `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"hint":"In Rails a sub-folder is a namespace (Render::Json)."}`. Rails sorts these by type on purpose, and a sub-folder is a namespace that changes every constant in it.

Sources:

- [Rails guides: autoloading and namespaces (Zeitwerk)](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/autoloading_and_reloading_constants.html)
- [Rails guides: migrations (db/migrate, timestamped)](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_migrations.html)

## php

PHP with Composer (Laravel, Symfony): a folder is a PSR-4 namespace and there is one class per file, hence 20. Laravel sorts app/Models and app/Http/Controllers by type, so they get more room. UserTest is User.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules","hint":"A folder is a PSR-4 namespace."}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"hint":"A folder is a PSR-4 namespace."}`
- **Companions:** `Test$`
- **Left out:** `storage`, `bootstrap/cache`, `public/build`
- **In `app/Models`, `app/Http/Controllers`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":40}`. Laravel sorts these by type by default.

Sources:

- [PSR-4: autoloading](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-4/)
- [Laravel: directory structure](https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/structure)

## c-cpp

C and C++: foo.h, foo.cc and foo_test.cc are one module. Without namespaces in C, a shared prefix is often the subsystem's name on purpose (Google: "http_server_logs.h rather than logs.h"), so groups are warnings and need five. Generated Qt and protobuf files are left out.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules"}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"min":5,"hint":"In C a shared prefix is often the subsystem's namespace: move them only if the subsystem deserves a directory."}`
- **Companions:** `[-_]inl$`, `_(test|unittest|tests)$`, `^test_`
- **Left out:** `cmake-build-*`, `/out`, `extern`, `/deps`, `*.pb.h`, `*.pb.cc`, `moc_*`, `ui_*`, `qrc_*`, `.vs`

Sources:

- [Google C++ style guide: file names](https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html)
- [Pitchfork: a C++ project layout](https://github.com/vector-of-bool/pitchfork)

## unity

Unity: every asset has a .meta next to it (Player.cs and Player.cs.meta are one), numbered series such as Model1, Model2 are one asset family, and Library, Temp, Packages and third-party plugins are left out. C# reads as in the dotnet preset.

- **Extends:** [dotnet](#dotnet)
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"min":15,"hint":"Allar's rule 2.7, the one number game guides give: \"If you find yourself having 15+ of these assets that belong together, they should be together.\""}`
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":30,"count":"modules"}`
- **Companions:** `_?\d+$`
- **Left out:** `!*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,webp,avif,ico,icns,bmp,tif,tiff,psd,xcf,exr,hdr,mp3,wav,ogg,flac,m4a,aac,mp4,webm,mov,avi,mkv,ttf,otf,woff,woff2,eot,pdf}`, `/Library`, `/Temp`, `/Logs`, `/UserSettings`, `/Packages`, `Assets/Plugins`, `*~`

Sources:

- [Unity manual: asset metadata (.meta files)](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/AssetMetadata.html)
- [Unity manual: special folder names](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/SpecialFolders.html)
- [Unity: best practices for organizing your project](https://unity.com/how-to/organizing-your-project)

## unreal

Unreal Engine, after Allar's style guide: an asset is named Prefix_BaseAssetName_Variant_Suffix, the prefix is its type and the base asset name is its group. Prefixes and texture suffixes (_D, _N, _ORM…) are skipped, so SM_Rock, T_Rock_D and M_Rock are all about Rock — and 15 or more of them get their own folder (guide rule 2.7). The guide sets no maximum per folder; 50 here is an opinion.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `warn` `{"max":50,"count":"modules"}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"min":15,"hint":"Allar 2.7: \"If you find yourself having 15+ of these assets that belong together, they should be together.\""}`
- **Companions:** `_(D|N|R|A|O|B|E|M|S|H|L|ORM|MRA|ARM|RMA)$`, `_(P|Audio|Lighting|Geo|Gameplay)$`, `_(Cue|Decal|Color|Table|Float|Vector|SC|Component|Context)$`, `_\d+$`
- **Leading words skipped:** `a`, `abp`, `ac`, `ai`, `aic`, `am`, `ao`, `att`, `bb`, `bp`, `bpfl`, `bpi`, `bpml`, `bs`, `bt`, `ca`, `cue`, `curve`, `dm`, `dt`, `dv`, `dw`, `e`, `eqs`, `f`, `ffe`, `fms`, `font`, `ft`, `lg`, `ll`, `ls`, `m`, `matinee`, `mf`, `mi`, `mp`, `mpc`, `msw`, `mt`, `ne`, `ns`, `ol`, `pfb`, `phys`, `pm`, `pp`, `ps`, `rig`, `rt`, `rtc`, `s`, `sgi`, `sif`, `sk`, `skel`, `sm`, `sp`, `spr`, `sprg`, `ss`, `t`, `tbp`, `tc`, `ti`, `tm`, `ts`, `vf`, `vfa`, `wbp`, `u`, `i`
- **Left out:** `!*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,webp,avif,ico,icns,bmp,tif,tiff,psd,xcf,exr,hdr,mp3,wav,ogg,flac,m4a,aac,mp4,webm,mov,avi,mkv,ttf,otf,woff,woff2,eot,pdf}`, `/Saved`, `/Intermediate`, `/DerivedDataCache`, `/Binaries`, `Content/Developers`, `.vs`

Sources:

- [Allar's UE5 style guide (1.2 asset names, 2.6, 2.7)](https://github.com/Allar/ue5-style-guide)

## godot

Godot: a scene and its script are one (player.tscn, player.gd), and so are the .import and .uid files next to an asset. Godot's guide asks to keep resources close to the scenes that use them — folders by feature. .godot and addons are left out.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"min":15,"hint":"Allar's rule 2.7, the one number game guides give: \"If you find yourself having 15+ of these assets that belong together, they should be together.\""}`
- **Left out:** `!*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,webp,avif,ico,icns,bmp,tif,tiff,psd,xcf,exr,hdr,mp3,wav,ogg,flac,m4a,aac,mp4,webm,mov,avi,mkv,ttf,otf,woff,woff2,eot,pdf}`, `.godot`, `/addons`

Sources:

- [Godot: project organization](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/best_practices/project_organization.html)
- [Godot 4.4: .uid files](https://godotengine.org/article/uid-changes-coming-to-godot-4-4/)

## terraform

Terraform: a folder is a module, and HashiCorp's style guide grows a configuration with more flat files (network.tf, storage.tf) before making one. Looser limits, and groups are warnings that ask whether they are a child module.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":25,"count":"modules","hint":"In Terraform a folder is a module."}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"hint":"In Terraform a folder is a module: would they be a child module under modules/?"}`
- **Left out:** `.terraform`

Sources:

- [Terraform: standard module structure](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/modules/develop/structure)
- [Terraform: style guide (file names)](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/style)

## docs

Documentation and content sites (Docusaurus, MkDocs, VitePress, Starlight, Astro, Hugo, Jekyll): number prefixes order pages and are not a group, and moving a page changes its URL, so groups in docs/, doc/, content/ and blog/ are warnings that say so; the code next to them keeps its rules. A blog's posts are a dated collection, not a drawer: _posts/, blog/ and content/posts are left as they are. Versioned copies, translations and build output are left out.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Left out:** `versioned_docs`, `versioned_sidebars`, `/i18n`, `.docusaurus`, `/site`, `/build`, `resources/_gen`
- **In `**/docs`, `**/docs/**`, `**/doc`, `**/doc/**`, `**/content`, `**/content/**`, `**/blog`, `**/blog/**`:** `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"hint":"Moving pages changes their URLs: add redirects."}`. A page is a URL: grouping pages into a folder breaks links unless redirects are added, so it is a warning that says so.
- **In `**/_posts`, `**/_drafts`, `**/blog`, `**/content/posts`, `**/content/blog`:** `max-files` `off`, `prefix-groups` `off`. A blog is a dated collection ("YEAR-MONTH-DAY-title" in Jekyll): it is read by date, not arranged by name, and it grows by design.

Sources:

- [Docusaurus: autogenerated sidebars and number prefixes](https://docusaurus.io/docs/sidebar/autogenerated)
- [MkDocs: writing your docs](https://www.mkdocs.org/user-guide/writing-your-docs/)
- [VitePress: file-based routing](https://vitepress.dev/guide/routing)
- [Starlight: pages](https://starlight.astro.build/guides/pages/)
- [Hugo: content organization, "A content's path is determined by the section's path to the file"](https://gohugo.io/content-management/organization/)
- [Jekyll: posts, "The _posts folder is where your blog posts live", named YEAR-MONTH-DAY-title](https://jekyllrb.com/docs/posts/)
- [Astro: content collections, "a set of related, structurally identical data"](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/)

## data-science

Data science projects laid out like cookiecutter-data-science: notebooks/ is flat and ordered by step (1.0-initials-description.ipynb), so it is not asked to split; data, models and figures are artefacts and are left out; the package under src/ reads as Python.

- **Extends:** [python](#python)
- **Left out:** `/data`, `/models`, `reports/figures`, `/references`, `.ipynb_checkpoints`
- **In `notebooks`, `notebooks/**`:** `max-files` `off`, `prefix-groups` `off`. Notebooks are numbered by step and kept flat on purpose: the number is the order.

Sources:

- [Cookiecutter Data Science: opinions and notebook naming](https://cookiecutter-data-science.drivendata.org/opinions/)

## latex

LaTeX books and theses: chapters stay together, figures get more room (many per chapter is normal) and fig-ch3-* files grouping into figures/ch3 is a warning. Build output is left out. An opinion: LaTeX has no guide on folders.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules"}`
- **Left out:** `_minted*`, `svg-inkscape`, `/build`, `/out`
- **In `**/figures`, `**/figs`, `**/images`, `**/img`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":40}`, `prefix-groups` `warn`. Many figures per chapter is normal.

Sources:

- [LaTeX Beginner's Guide: splitting a document into files](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/latex-beginners-guide/9781847199867/ch10.html)
